newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's banking activity up in November.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's banking activity up in November.

text.p: The consolidated balance sheet of Lebanon's commercial banks registered a monthly rise of 2.9 percent in November to 35,784 billion Lebanese pounds ($23.1 billion), the Bank of Lebanon said in its latest monthly bulletin on Tuesday.
Total deposits in foreign currencies and Lebanese pounds rose 2.78 percent to 29,870 billion pounds from 29,062 billion in October, it said.
Lebanese pound deposits grew 3.49 percent to 12,978 billion pounds from 12,541 billion a month earlier.
Deposits in foreign currencies grew 2.37 percent to $10.870 billion in November from $10.618 billion in October, the Bank added.
Loans and credits to the private sector rose 2.43 percent in November over October, increasing to 12,480 billion pounds.
Credits in Lebanese pounds rose 2.00 percent in November to 1,570 billion pounds.
Credits in foreign currencies rose 2.63 percent to $7.020 billion from $6.841 billion a month earlier.
